9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium close-up, eye level, Scarlett (Image 2) faces the mirror with the lipstick near her mouth, a faint smile forming as she finishes applying the color., Scarlett (Image 2)’s reflection is centered in the mirror, coral lips vivid against the neutral bathroom; the phone and sunglasses sit low in the reflected foreground., downtown_apartment_bathroom_white_tile_black_stone, Hard, directional morning sunlight cuts across the white tile and sink, creating a crisp stripe of illumination and sharp reflected highlights. The rest of the room remains softly neutral by comparison., Glossy white, charcoal black, brushed chrome, pale gray, and vivid coral accent., scarlett_city_influencer, Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
